source.title: TimeROME-DLM: Temporal Causal Tracing and Low-Rank Inference-Time Knowledge Editing for Masked Diffusion Language Models
source.authors: Zheng-Tao Yao; Liuyang Song; Hongbo Zhang; Chen Wei; Haoyan Xu; Guang Yang; Si-Heng Wang

record.tranche_reason: Reports robustness results that qualify its inference-time editing method: paraphrasing has little stated effect, while in-context relearning weakens the edit.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports knowledge-editing efficacy, utility and causal-tracing results, but these do not test the specified recovery attacks. The attack findings are qualitative summaries; no separate attack values by model or prompt variant are stated.
record.test_reason: The study proposes an inference-time unlearning edit (TimeROME-DLM) for masked diffusion LMs, which is a new setting. It reports two prompting attacks on that edit: question/answer paraphrase and in-context relearning. These bear on version E (prompt-only recovery) and version F (a robust counter-method). The evidence is thin. The paraphrase number appears in one sentence (Section IV.E) and the in-context number in two (Section IV.E and Limitations item 3), alongside a radar chart (Fig. 5). There are no per-model values and no confidence intervals.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report that the edit holds within 2 nats under question/answer paraphrase across FT'd backbones but weakens by ~8 nats under in-context relearning. They call this a known vulnerability of forget-only methods and leave a hardened variant (e.g. adversarial training of the edit memory) to future work.
record.recipe_differences: TimeROME-DLM uses a training-free inference-time residual edit with frozen backbone weights, unlike gradient-based unlearning or weight-editing recipes; its robustness results concern attacks on that edit.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompt condition changes the reported outcome: paraphrasing has an effect within ∼2 nats, while in-context relearning weakens the edit by ∼8 nats.
record.code_released: not stated; artifacts are promised for release upon acceptance
record.problems: The attack findings are qualitative summaries without separate per-model or per-condition values or stated uncertainty. The in-context attack is reported as an approximately 8-nat weakening, which does not by itself establish how much knowledge is recovered relative to an unedited model.

untested.parts: Near-chance accuracy, kept utility and attack resistance are never measured together. WMDP-Bio accuracy (0.65 to 0.36 for TimeROME, 0.41 for Adaptive-RMU on an MDLM) is reported without any attack, and the attacks are run only on TOFU ForgetLP. No standard AR unlearning method is attacked.
No activation-direction ablation or hook-removal recovery test. The edit is reversible by design (the hook can be removed and the weights are untouched), but this is not tested as an attack.
Jailbreaks and other languages are not tested; only paraphrase and in-context answer presentation are.
Resistance to fine-tuning, internal ablation and quantization is not tested.

missing.what: Method efficacy and utility cost at the operating point probably used for the robustness tests. WMDP-Bio accuracy falls from 0.65 to 0.36 (chance 0.25), and at alpha=2, q=4 TOFU RetainLP falls from -34.8 to -89.1. Researchers need this to judge whether the method that resists the attacks actually forgets, and at what utility cost. It is the method's own performance, not an attack.

Which configuration (alpha, q) and which backbone the paraphrase (2-nat) and in-context relearning (~8-nat) figures refer to. Neither is stated, and the size of the edit they are measured against depends on it (about 6 to 83 nats in Table I).
missing.locator: Section IV.E Robustness; Section VI item 3; Fig. 5

record.verdict_notes: Changes from the previous verdict: (1) I merged the duplicate row_fixes items into one item per row, for both R1 (the flagged duplicate) and R2, which also had two. Each row keeps versions E and F. The state is read as recovery, E's effect: R1 is absent, which means resistance observed for F; R2 is partial, matching the earlier E and F states. (2) I added a caveat to R2 and to the second missing item: the robustness configuration is unstated, and at alpha=1, q=2 the edit is only ~6 nats, so the 'partial' reading assumes the ~83-nat headline configuration. That is the most likely one, since the ablations in the same section use -83 as the reference. (3) I reworded untested A to say that WMDP accuracy is never attacked and that the attacks are run only on TOFU ForgetLP. (4) I reworded the first missing item so it no longer attributes a 'forgets while keeping ability' premise to F, which the version text does not contain. (5) In test_reason I noted that the ~8-nat figure appears in two sentences, not one. Relation, tranche, labels, the other untested entries and authors_conclusion are otherwise unchanged. Context: the setting is masked diffusion LMs (LLaDA, Dream, MMaDA, DiffuLLaMA, LLaDA-MoE) with a training-free residual hook, not weight-level unlearning of AR models, so the verdicts apply only to this setting. Forgetting is measured as TOFU forget-set log-probability in nats, not accuracy, so 'restores knowledge' cannot be read directly. The abstract claims CIs 'on every cell', but the robustness results have none. The meaning of the dagger marks on many cells (Tables I-V, Fig. 5) is never fully explained. The one dagger row that is explained (Table V, k=100) is extrapolated, not measured, so dagger-marked values may not all be direct measurements. Not recorded under fits_no_version: the finding that gradient unlearning baselines (NPO, SimNPO, Adaptive-RMU, GA, GD) collapse MDLMs at standard learning rates or barely move the forget set. It is a baseline comparison about method transfer, not about recovery. No instructions were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report that an attack-resistant unlearning method both brings targeted knowledge to near chance and preserves general ability.
No fine-tuning or other training on a small relearning set is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or test of recovery by removing an internal edit is reported.
No low-bit quantization attack is tested.
Tests question or answer paraphrasing and in-context relearning only; jailbreaks and other languages are not reported.
Tests the proposed method against paraphrasing and in-context relearning only; resistance to fine-tuning, activation ablation and quantization attacks is not reported.

rows.check: Merged the earlier two items for R1 into one. The text says the edit holds 'within 2 nats under question or answer paraphrase across all FT'd backbones' (Section IV.E, Fig. 5). Against the ~83-nat headline edit that is no meaningful recovery, so the state, read as recovery (E's effect), is absent. For F the same number means the edit's resistance held, i.e. resistance is observed. Only an aggregate sentence and the radar chart support this. There are no separate question/answer or per-backbone values and no uncertainty, and the (alpha, q) configuration used is not stated.

rows.check: Merged the earlier two items for R2 into one. The locator is wrong: the result is in Section IV.E (Robustness) and Section VI item 3, with Fig. 5, not Section IV.C. Presenting the answer in-context just before the query weakens the edit by ~8 nats. Against the ~83-nat headline edit that is about a tenth recovered: a small partial recovery for E and partial resistance for F. The authors call it 'a known vulnerability of forget-only methods'. Caveat: the (alpha, q) and backbone are not stated. At alpha=1, q=2 the edit itself is only ~6 nats (Table I: -42.04 vs -35.70), and there 8 nats would be full recovery. The figure is not converted to accuracy and has no uncertainty.

relation.reason: The authors run paraphrase and in-context attacks on their own edit.

tranche.reason: A new setting (masked diffusion LM, own inference-time edit) with attack results bearing on E and F. The reader's T5 is not needed, since no argument says a version is wrong.

source_check.notes: Both attack results are one-sentence summaries pointing to the Fig. 5 radar chart, with no per-model values or uncertainty. The in-context result's model and configuration are unstated, so pairing it with the 83-nat headline is an inference. The synthesis cites R2 on both sides: E.against[9] as failure to restore, F.against[6] as reaching residual knowledge.

statements.correction: TimeROME edit, TOFU-finetuned masked diffusion LMs. Answer shown in context just before the query weakens the edit by ~8 nats. Model and configuration not stated. Headline edit effect: -83.24 nats on FT'd LLaDA-8B-Base. Authors call it a known vulnerability of forget-only methods. Record verdict: E limits_scope.
statements.problem: Cites R2 without naming the study. R2 gives the forgotten answer itself in context, which the conditions say is mostly excluded. It is a masked diffusion LM on TOFU, not a 3-8B AR LLM. It is a partial weakening that the authors call a vulnerability, and the record's E verdict for R2 is limits_scope, not challenges.
Cites R1 without naming the study, but the implied placement fits. It is an own-method test on masked diffusion LMs, and paraphrase gives no recovery.
none. The study does present the answer in context for a TimeROME edit in masked diffusion LMs.

statements.correction: TimeROME: frozen backbone, inference-time residual edit hook. TOFU-finetuned masked diffusion LMs (LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B and others). Only question/answer paraphrase tested. The edit holds within 2 nats. No per-model values or uncertainty for this result.
statements.problem: Cites R1 without naming the study. The frozen-weight, added-component frame fits. But the stated models (1B-8B Llama, Qwen distill, Gemma), the 'all four' and the attack list (jailbreaks, translations, SFT) do not cover this study.
Cites R1 without naming the study. R1 fits the prompt-level paraphrase on masked diffusion LM condition, and the edit holds within 2 nats. The EMDU numbers belong to another paper.
